meta.title: One-Year Bible Journey
meta.notes: Sundays are deep-dive/catch-up days and have no reading.

phases.name: Divided kingdom, prophets, exile and return

weeks.title: Creation and the early world
weeks.deepDive: Find the Tigris and Euphrates on a map; this is the world of Genesis 1–11. Watch BibleProject’s Genesis 1–11 overview. Note: Job is placed here because its setting resembles the age of the patriarchs.

memoryVerse.textKJV: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

weeks.title: The book of Job
weeks.deepDive: Write one paragraph: what do Job’s friends get wrong about suffering, and how does God answer?

memoryVerse.textKJV: For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth.

weeks.title: Abraham’s call
weeks.deepDive: Trace Abraham’s journey: Ur to Harran to Canaan to Egypt and back. Note what God promises him; it drives the whole Bible.

memoryVerse.textKJV: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.

weeks.title: Isaac, Jacob, and the twelve sons
weeks.deepDive: Draw a family tree from Abraham to Jacob’s 12 sons. These sons become the 12 tribes of Israel.

memoryVerse.textKJV: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.

weeks.title: Joseph in Egypt; the Exodus begins
weeks.deepDive: Locate Egypt, the Nile, and Goshen. Read about how Joseph’s family ends up enslaved generations later.

memoryVerse.textKJV: But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

weeks.title: Passover, the Red Sea, and Sinai
weeks.deepDive: Look at a map of possible Exodus routes and locations proposed for Mount Sinai. Learn the 10 Commandments in order.

memoryVerse.textKJV: I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

weeks.title: The Tabernacle; Leviticus begins
weeks.deepDive: Sketch the Tabernacle layout: courtyard, Holy Place, Most Holy Place. Watch BibleProject’s Leviticus overview.

memoryVerse.textKJV: And the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth.

weeks.title: Holiness and sacrifice
weeks.deepDive: Study the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16). What were clean/unclean laws for? You’ll meet these ideas again in Hebrews.

memoryVerse.textKJV: Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the LORD.

weeks.title: Numbers: Israel organized
weeks.deepDive: Draw how the 12 tribes camped around the Tabernacle (Numbers 2).

memoryVerse.textKJV: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee: The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.

weeks.title: Forty years in the wilderness
weeks.deepDive: Map Kadesh, Edom, and the plains of Moab. Why did Israel wander 40 years?

memoryVerse.textKJV: God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?

weeks.title: Deuteronomy: Moses’ final speeches
weeks.deepDive: Learn what a covenant is. Ancient Near Eastern treaties had a similar structure to Deuteronomy.

memoryVerse.textKJV: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD: And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.

weeks.title: Moses’ farewell
weeks.deepDive: Phase 1 review: write the story from creation to Moses’ death in 10 sentences. Review verses 1–12.

memoryVerse.textKJV: Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.

weeks.title: Joshua and the conquest
weeks.deepDive: Map the tribal territories (Joshua 13–21). Who were the Canaanites and what did they worship?

memoryVerse.textKJV: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.

weeks.title: The judges
weeks.deepDive: Chart the repeating cycle in Judges: sin, oppression, cry for help, a judge rescues. Who were the Philistines?

memoryVerse.textKJV: In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.

weeks.title: Ruth; Samuel; the Psalms begin
weeks.deepDive: Ruth is a Moabite (a foreigner) who becomes David’s great-grandmother. Find Moab and Bethlehem on a map.

memoryVerse.textKJV: And Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God.

weeks.title: Saul falls, David rises
weeks.deepDive: Find the Valley of Elah, where David fought Goliath. Read Psalm 23 slowly as David’s song.

memoryVerse.textKJV: But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the Lord seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.

weeks.title: David on the run
weeks.deepDive: Map David’s hideouts (En Gedi, the wilderness of Judah). Many psalms’ headings tie them to these events; look for them.

memoryVerse.textKJV: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.

weeks.title: Saul’s death; Chronicles’ family trees
weeks.deepDive: Learn why Chronicles retells Samuel–Kings: it was written after the exile to remind the returned Jews of their roots. Skim the genealogies.

memoryVerse.textKJV: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.

weeks.title: David becomes king; Jerusalem
weeks.deepDive: Look at a map of Jerusalem’s City of David. Why did David choose Jerusalem as his capital?

memoryVerse.textKJV: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.

weeks.title: God’s promise to David
weeks.deepDive: Study the Davidic covenant (2 Samuel 7). This is why Jesus is called “Son of David” in the Gospels.

memoryVerse.textKJV: And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.

weeks.title: David’s sin and its fallout
weeks.deepDive: Read 2 Samuel 11–12 again with Psalm 51. How does the Bible treat its heroes’ failures?

memoryVerse.textKJV: As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us.

weeks.title: Absalom’s revolt; the Songs of Ascent
weeks.deepDive: Psalms 120–134 are “Songs of Ascent,” sung by pilgrims walking up to Jerusalem for festivals. Read a few aloud.

memoryVerse.textKJV: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

weeks.title: David’s last days; Proverbs begins
weeks.deepDive: Map the extent of the kingdom under David and Solomon, its largest ever.

memoryVerse.textKJV: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.

weeks.title: Solomon’s wisdom and Temple
weeks.deepDive: Look up a diagram of Solomon’s Temple and compare it with your Tabernacle sketch from Week 7.

memoryVerse.textKJV: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.

weeks.title: Solomon’s peak and decline
weeks.deepDive: Read 1 Kings 11 again: how did Solomon’s foreign alliances and wives set up the kingdom’s split?

memoryVerse.textKJV: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.

weeks.title: Song of Songs and Ecclesiastes
weeks.deepDive: Phase 2 review: list the kings Saul, David, Solomon and one key event for each. Review verses 13–26.

memoryVerse.textKJV: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.

weeks.title: The kingdom splits; Elijah
weeks.deepDive: Map the two kingdoms: Israel (north, capital Samaria) and Judah (south, capital Jerusalem). Who was Baal?

memoryVerse.textKJV: And Elijah came unto all the people, and said, How long halt ye between two opinions? if the LORD be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.

weeks.title: Elisha; Joel; Jonah
weeks.deepDive: Find Nineveh, Assyria’s capital, on a map. Assyria is the superpower rising in this period.

memoryVerse.textKJV: And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions.

weeks.title: Amos, Hosea, Micah; the north falls
weeks.deepDive: Read 2 Kings 17: Assyria destroys Israel in 722 BC and resettles foreigners there. This is where the Samaritans come from.

memoryVerse.textKJV: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?

weeks.title: Hezekiah; Isaiah begins
weeks.deepDive: Look up Hezekiah’s tunnel and Sennacherib’s prism, real archaeological finds tied to 2 Kings 18–20.

memoryVerse.textKJV: Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.

weeks.title: Isaiah: judgment and comfort
weeks.deepDive: Isaiah 40 onward speaks to exiles in Babylon. Learn why some scholars think later authors wrote these chapters, and why others disagree.

memoryVerse.textKJV: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.

weeks.title: Isaiah ends; Josiah; Babylon rises
weeks.deepDive: Nineveh falls in 612 BC (Nahum) and Babylon becomes the new superpower. Read Isaiah 53 and note how the New Testament uses it.

memoryVerse.textKJV: But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.

weeks.title: Jeremiah warns Judah
weeks.deepDive: List the last kings of Judah (Josiah, Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin, Zedekiah) and how Jeremiah dealt with each.

memoryVerse.textKJV: Blessed is the man that trusteth in the LORD, and whose hope the LORD is.

weeks.title: Jeremiah: the new covenant
weeks.deepDive: Read Jeremiah 29 in full: this famous verse was a letter to exiles told to settle in Babylon for 70 years. Then read 31:31–34.

memoryVerse.textKJV: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.

weeks.title: Jerusalem falls; Ezekiel begins
weeks.deepDive: Map the route from Jerusalem to Babylon. Imagine losing the Temple: how does Lamentations express that grief?

memoryVerse.textKJV: It is of the LORD’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.

weeks.title: Ezekiel’s visions
weeks.deepDive: Find Tyre on a map (Ezekiel 26–28). Watch BibleProject’s Ezekiel overview.

memoryVerse.textKJV: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh.

weeks.title: Dry bones; Daniel
weeks.deepDive: Read Daniel 2 and 7: the sequence of empires (Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece, and a fourth). Persia conquers Babylon in 539 BC.

memoryVerse.textKJV: If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.

weeks.title: The return; Temple rebuilt; Esther
weeks.deepDive: Look up the Cyrus Cylinder and a map of the Persian Empire. Learn the story behind the Jewish festival of Purim (Esther).

memoryVerse.textKJV: Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the LORD unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.

weeks.title: Ezra, Nehemiah, Malachi
weeks.deepDive: Study the 400 years between the Testaments: Alexander, the Maccabees and Hanukkah, Rome’s arrival, and the rise of Pharisees and Sadducees. Review verses 27–39.

memoryVerse.textKJV: Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the LORD is your strength.

weeks.title: The Gospel of Mark
weeks.deepDive: Map Galilee, Samaria, and Judea in Jesus’ day. Learn the Herod family: who ruled what.

memoryVerse.textKJV: And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.

weeks.title: Matthew: the Sermon on the Mount
weeks.deepDive: Matthew was written with Jewish readers in mind. Count how often he says a prophecy was “fulfilled.”

memoryVerse.textKJV: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

weeks.title: Matthew: the final week
weeks.deepDive: Jesus quotes Deuteronomy 6:5 and Leviticus 19:18, both verses you’ve memorized. Make a day-by-day timeline of Holy Week.

memoryVerse.textKJV: Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

weeks.title: Luke: Jesus and the outsiders
weeks.deepDive: Read the Good Samaritan (Luke 10) again knowing who Samaritans were. Jesus’ hearers would have been shocked.

memoryVerse.textKJV: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised.

weeks.title: Luke ends; John begins
weeks.deepDive: Compare one event (like the feeding of the 5,000) across all four Gospels. What does each emphasize?

memoryVerse.textKJV: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

weeks.title: John: the “I am” sayings
weeks.deepDive: List John’s seven “I am” statements. Learn about the Feast of Tabernacles (John 7).

memoryVerse.textKJV: Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

weeks.title: The church is born
weeks.deepDive: Acts 1:8 is the map of the book: Jerusalem, Judea and Samaria, the ends of the earth. Read Acts 10: the first Gentile convert.

memoryVerse.textKJV: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judæa, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.

weeks.title: Jerusalem Council; Paul’s journeys
weeks.deepDive: Map Paul’s first and second journeys. Acts 15 settles whether Gentiles must follow Jewish law.

memoryVerse.textKJV: There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.

weeks.title: Corinth
weeks.deepDive: Learn about Corinth: a wealthy, diverse Roman port city. How does that explain the church’s problems?

memoryVerse.textKJV: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil.

weeks.title: Romans
weeks.deepDive: Read Romans 9–11: Paul’s answer to how Jews and Gentiles fit into God’s plan.

memoryVerse.textKJV: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.

weeks.title: Paul’s arrest; letters from prison
weeks.deepDive: Map Paul’s voyage to Rome (Acts 27). Why did his Roman citizenship matter?

memoryVerse.textKJV: I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.

weeks.title: Letters to churches and leaders
weeks.deepDive: Learn about Nero’s persecution, the traditional deaths of Peter and Paul, and Rome’s destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70.

memoryVerse.textKJV: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness.

weeks.title: Hebrews, John’s letters, Revelation
weeks.deepDive: Map the seven churches of Revelation (modern Turkey). Notice how Revelation borrows images from Daniel and Ezekiel. Final review: all 52 verses.

memoryVerse.textKJV: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.

eras.title: Creation and the patriarchs
eras.keyPeople: Adam, Noah, Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph
eras.summary: From the garden to Abraham’s call out of Ur. God promises Abraham a land, many descendants, and blessing for all nations.

eras.title: Egypt and the Exodus
eras.summary: Jacob’s family grows into a nation enslaved in Egypt. Moses leads them out, God gives the Law at Sinai, and they wander 40 years.

eras.title: Conquest and the judges
eras.summary: Israel settles Canaan tribe by tribe, then cycles through unfaithfulness and rescue by local leaders called judges.

eras.title: The united kingdom
eras.summary: Israel asks for a king. David makes Jerusalem the capital and receives God’s promise of an everlasting dynasty. Solomon builds the Temple.

eras.title: Two kingdoms
eras.keyPeople: Elijah, Elisha, Ahab, Jezebel, Jonah, Amos, Hosea
eras.summary: The kingdom splits: Israel in the north, Judah in the south. Prophets confront Baal worship and injustice. Assyria destroys the north in 722 BC.

eras.title: Judah alone
eras.keyPeople: Hezekiah, Isaiah, Micah, Josiah, Jeremiah, Habakkuk
eras.summary: Judah survives Assyria’s siege of Jerusalem, then falls to Babylon. The Temple is destroyed in 586 BC.

eras.title: Exile in Babylon
eras.summary: Jews live as captives in Babylon, wrestling with how God can be present without the Temple.

eras.title: Return and rebuilding
eras.keyPeople: Cyrus, Zerubbabel, Haggai, Zechariah, Esther, Ezra, Nehemiah, Malachi
eras.summary: Persia conquers Babylon and lets the exiles go home. They rebuild the Temple and Jerusalem’s walls.

eras.title: Between the Testaments
eras.keyPeople: Alexander the Great, the Maccabees, Herod the Great
eras.summary: No biblical books cover these centuries in most Protestant Bibles. Greek culture spreads, the Maccabees revolt (the origin of Hanukkah), and Rome takes over in 63 BC. Pharisees and Sadducees emerge.

eras.title: The life of Jesus
eras.keyPeople: Mary, John the Baptist, the Twelve, Pontius Pilate, Herod Antipas
eras.summary: Jesus teaches in Galilee and Judea, announcing God’s kingdom, and is crucified in Jerusalem under Roman rule.

eras.title: The early church
eras.keyPeople: Peter, Paul, Barnabas, James, Timothy, John
eras.summary: The movement spreads from Jerusalem across the Roman world. Gentiles join in large numbers. Rome destroys Jerusalem in AD 70.

peoples.name: Hebrews
peoples.desc: Abraham’s descendants; the oldest name for the people, often used by outsiders.

peoples.name: Israelites
peoples.desc: The 12 tribes descended from Jacob, who was renamed Israel.

peoples.name: Israel (northern kingdom)
peoples.desc: Ten tribes that split off after Solomon, capital Samaria. Conquered by Assyria in 722 BC.

peoples.name: Judah (southern kingdom)
peoples.desc: The tribes of Judah and Benjamin, capital Jerusalem, ruled by David’s descendants.

peoples.name: Jews
peoples.desc: From “Judah”: those who survived the Babylonian exile. The main name by New Testament times.

peoples.name: Gentiles
peoples.desc: Everyone who isn’t Jewish (“the nations”). How Gentiles join God’s people is a central New Testament question.

peoples.name: Samaritans
peoples.desc: Descendants of northern Israelites mixed with peoples Assyria resettled there. Bitter rivals of the Jews.

peoples.name: Canaanites
peoples.desc: Inhabitants of the land before Israel; worshipped Baal and Asherah.

peoples.name: Philistines
peoples.desc: Seafaring people on the southwest coast; Israel’s rival under Saul and David (Goliath).

peoples.name: Moabites, Edomites, Ammonites
peoples.desc: Neighbors east of the Jordan, related by ancestry (Lot, Esau). Ruth was a Moabite.

peoples.name: Pharisees
peoples.desc: A popular Jewish movement devoted to careful keeping of the Law, including oral tradition.

peoples.name: Sadducees
peoples.desc: The priestly elite who ran the Temple; accepted only the written Law and denied resurrection.

prophets.name: Zephaniah, Habakkuk
prophets.message: Babylon is coming; live by faith
